subject: The journey from kitchen survey to fitting
hook: Have these decided and your kitchen survey goes twice as far
ig:
Have these decided and your kitchen survey goes twice as far.

A bespoke kitchen goes through a few clear stages. Each one runs more smoothly if you've made certain decisions first:

Before the survey: a wish list. What you love, what drives you mad and how many people cook at once.

At the survey: which walls, windows and doors are fixed, and roughly where you want the sink and hob.

Before design sign-off: appliance make and model numbers. Integrated appliances dictate exact housing sizes.

Before manufacture: finish, handles and worktop confirmed. After cutting, changes get harder.

Before fitting: room cleared, removal of the old kitchen agreed, and any gas, electrical or plumbing work booked.

If the summer holidays are your planning time, this is a good week to start the wish list.

Save this for later, and book a free design consultation through the link in bio.
fb:
Thinking about a new kitchen and using the summer to plan it? Here's what helps at each stage.

Before we survey, jot down a wish list and what annoys you about the current kitchen. At the survey, know which walls and windows are fixed. Before signing off the design, have your appliance model numbers ready, because integrated appliances set exact sizes. Confirm finishes and handles before we cut anything. And before fitting, get the room cleared and any gas, electrics or plumbing booked.
